Session Management.Greetings & SmallTalk: This topic includes conversations at the start or end of the session, greetings, casual small talk, or polite exchanges. Example patient statements: 'Hi, how are you?', 'It’s good to see you again,' 'See you next week.'
Session Management.CheckIn & WellbeingInquiry: This topic includes conversations where the therapist or patient checks in on current wellbeing, general state, or mood. Example patient statements: 'I’m doing okay today,' 'I feel tired but fine,' 'How are you?'

Personal Background & Identity.ChildhoodFamilyDynamics & ChildhoodExper: This topic includes conversations about family dynamics during childhood, early upbringing, supportive or neglectful parenting, positive memories, or difficult experiences such as abuse. Example patient statements: 'I had a happy childhood with my parents,' 'I grew up feeling unsupported,' 'My childhood shaped who I am today.'
Personal Background & Identity.CulturalBackground & ReligiousBeliefs: This topic includes conversations about cultural identity, ethnic background, religious or spiritual beliefs, migration experiences, and how these shape a person positively or negatively. Example patient statements: 'I’m proud of my cultural heritage,' 'Religion gives me comfort,' 'I feel disconnected from my cultural roots.'
Personal Background & Identity.EducationLevel & WorkHistory: This topic includes conversations about education, academic background, work history, job satisfaction, achievements, unemployment, or challenges in finding work. Example patient statements: 'I loved school and did well,' 'I’m proud of my degree,' 'I’ve struggled to hold a steady job.'
Personal Background & Identity.ValuesBeliefs & LongTermLifeGoals: This topic includes conversations about personal values, guiding beliefs, life goals, dreams, and hopes for the future, whether clear or uncertain. Example patient statements: 'Family is the most important value in my life,' 'I have big dreams for the future,' 'I feel like I have no direction.'
Personal Background & Identity.StrengthsSkills & PersonalGrowth: This topic includes conversations about personal strengths, skills, talents, growth, empowerment, or struggles with confidence. Example patient statements: 'I’m good at solving problems,' 'I’ve grown a lot in recent years,' 'I don’t feel like I have many strengths.'
Personal Background & Identity.SelfPerceptionIdentity & SelfEsteem: This topic includes conversations about self-perception, identity, self-esteem, self-compassion, pride in oneself, or struggles with self-worth. Example patient statements: 'I’m proud of who I am,' 'I feel comfortable in my own skin,' 'I don’t know who I really am.'

Relationships.CurrentParentRelations & FamilyInteracti: This topic includes conversations about current relationships with parents or family, whether supportive, close, estranged, or conflicted. Example patient statements: 'My father and I are very close,' 'I don’t talk to my family anymore,' 'Family gatherings make me happy.'
Relationships.RomanticRelationships & SexualRelationsh: This topic includes conversations about romantic and sexual relationships, intimacy, dating, long-term partnerships, positive experiences, or difficulties such as breakups or trust issues. Example patient statements: 'My partner makes me feel safe,' 'My last relationship ended badly,' 'I enjoy dating.'
Relationships.Friendships & SocialSupport: This topic includes conversations about friendships, social connections, networks of support, loneliness, or isolation. Example patient statements: 'I have a few close friends I can rely on,' 'I feel lonely most of the time,' 'My friends support me when I need them.'
Relationships.PeerColleagueRelations: This topic includes conversations about relationships with peers, colleagues, supervisors, or academic connections, both positive and challenging. Example patient statements: 'I get along well with my coworkers,' 'I feel judged at work,' 'School friends were always supportive.'
Relationships.ConflictLoss & AbuseHistory: This topic includes conversations about interpersonal conflict, reconciliation, loss, grief, or experiences of abuse. Example patient statements: 'I had a fight with a friend but we made up,' 'Losing my grandmother was very hard,' 'I was emotionally abused growing up.'
Relationships.BoundariesCommunication & RecurringDynam: This topic includes conversations about setting boundaries, communication styles, recurring dynamics in relationships, positive communication, or difficulties like idealization and devaluation. Example patient statements: 'I’ve learned to say no when needed,' 'I struggle with healthy boundaries,' 'I either idolize people or cut them off.'

Mental & Emotional Life.MainSymptoms & EmotionalReactions: This topic includes conversations about mood and emotions, such as joy, excitement, calmness, sadness, anger, or instability. Example patient statements: 'I’ve been feeling happy and balanced lately,' 'I get angry too easily,' 'My emotions change quickly.'
Mental & Emotional Life.ThoughtsWorriesRumination & CognitiveSty: This topic includes conversations about thinking patterns, whether optimistic, rational, creative, or negative, anxious, or accusatory. Example patient statements: 'I tend to think positively,' 'I overthink everything,' 'I believe people are against me sometimes.'
Mental & Emotional Life.CopingStrategies & DefenseMechanisms: This topic includes conversations about coping strategies and defense mechanisms, whether adaptive (exercise, journaling, relaxation) or maladaptive (avoidance, projection, denial). Example patient statements: 'I cope well with stress by exercising,' 'I avoid problems until it’s too late.'
Mental & Emotional Life.SelfPerceptionIdentity & IdentityStruggl: This topic includes conversations about identity, self-image, self-esteem, and confidence, whether stable and positive or unstable and negative. Example patient statements: 'I feel comfortable with who I am,' 'My self-image changes constantly,' 'I often feel worthless.'
Mental & Emotional Life.TraumaAdverseExperiences & AbuseHistory: This topic includes conversations about past trauma, adversity, or abuse, as well as resilience, recovery, or positive reinterpretation of difficult events. Example patient statements: 'I was abused as a child,' 'I’ve learned to grow from past trauma,' 'Hardships made me stronger.'
Mental & Emotional Life.GriefLoss & TerminatedRelationships: This topic includes conversations about grief, mourning, and loss, or finding meaning after losing someone or something important. Example patient statements: 'I’m still grieving my loss,' 'I’ve found peace after my breakup,' 'Losing friends has made me appreciate the ones I still have.'

Behavior & Habits.DailyRoutines & Lifestyle: This topic includes conversations about daily routines, lifestyle choices, and structure, whether stable and healthy or chaotic and unstructured. Example patient statements: 'I follow a healthy daily routine,' 'My days have no structure,' 'I rarely leave the house.'
Behavior & Habits.SleepPatterns & EatingHabits: This topic includes conversations about sleep quality, rest, eating habits, appetite, and nutrition, whether balanced or problematic. Example patient statements: 'I sleep well most nights,' 'I can’t fall asleep easily,' 'I forget to eat when stressed.'
Behavior & Habits.SubstanceAbuse: This topic includes conversations about alcohol, drugs, or other substances, whether absent, moderate, or problematic. Example patient statements: 'I don’t drink or use drugs,' 'I enjoy wine with dinner,' 'I rely on substances when stressed.'
Behavior & Habits.SelfHarmSuicidality & ImpulsiveRiskBehav: This topic includes conversations about self-harm, suicidality, or impulsive and risky behaviors, as well as discussions of safety, resilience, and recovery. Example patient statements: 'I’ve never harmed myself,' 'Sometimes I cut when I feel overwhelmed,' 'I take risks without thinking.'
Behavior & Habits.ExerciseHealthBehaviors: This topic includes conversations about exercise, health habits, and physical activity, whether absent, occasional, or regular. Example patient statements: 'I exercise every day,' 'I don’t work out much,' 'My lifestyle is sedentary.'
Behavior & Habits.ProductivityProcrastination: This topic includes conversations about productivity, procrastination, motivation, and time management, whether effective or impaired. Example patient statements: 'I manage my time well,' 'I procrastinate on everything,' 'I’m motivated to complete tasks.'

WorkStudyFinances.WorkHistory & JobSatisfaction: This topic includes conversations about work history, employment, unemployment, job satisfaction, achievements, or burnout. Example patient statements: 'I’m proud of my career,' 'I’ve been unemployed for months,' 'I love my job.'
WorkStudyFinances.AcademicChallenges: This topic includes conversations about academic performance, studies, and education, whether positive or negative. Example patient statements: 'I did well in school,' 'I struggled academically,' 'I enjoy studying new things.'
WorkStudyFinances.CareerChoicesTransitions: This topic includes conversations about career choices, transitions, and professional growth, whether smooth or stressful. Example patient statements: 'I’m excited about my career change,' 'I don’t know what path to take,' 'My career transition was difficult.'
WorkStudyFinances.FinancialSituation: This topic includes conversations about finances, money management, financial stability, or stress. Example patient statements: 'I’m financially stable,' 'I live paycheck to paycheck,' 'I’m worried about money.'

HealthBody.PreexistingConditions & CurrentMedicatio: This topic includes conversations about physical health conditions, medical history, and medication use, whether stable, absent, or challenging. Example patient statements: 'I have no major health problems,' 'I take antidepressants,' 'My medication helps sometimes.'
HealthBody.PainChronicConditions: This topic includes conversations about chronic pain or ongoing physical health conditions, whether well-managed or disruptive. Example patient statements: 'I don’t have chronic pain,' 'My pain is manageable,' 'I’ve suffered from back pain for years.'
HealthBody.BodyImageEatingHabits: This topic includes conversations about body image, appearance, eating habits, and nutrition, whether healthy or troubled. Example patient statements: 'I’m happy with how I look,' 'I don’t like my body,' 'I sometimes restrict my eating.'
HealthBody.SexualHealth: This topic includes conversations about sexual health, functioning, and wellbeing, whether satisfying or problematic. Example patient statements: 'I’m comfortable with my sexuality,' 'Sex makes me anxious,' 'I struggle with sexual health issues.'
HealthBody.MedicalAdherence & MedicationResponse: This topic includes conversations about adherence to medical treatments, following prescriptions, and responses to medication, whether positive or negative. Example patient statements: 'I always take my meds as prescribed,' 'I forget sometimes,' 'The medication only helps partially.'

SocialEnvironmentalContext.HousingStability & HousingConditions: This topic includes conversations about housing, living arrangements, stability, and conditions, whether positive or insecure. Example patient statements: 'I love my home,' 'I live alone and feel isolated,' 'I’m worried about losing my apartment.'
SocialEnvironmentalContext.CommunityPolitics & SocialCohesion: This topic includes conversations about community ties, political environment, social cohesion, and belonging, whether supportive or lacking. Example patient statements: 'I feel supported by my community,' 'My neighborhood is unsafe,' 'I don’t trust politics here.'
SocialEnvironmentalContext.SocialSupportNetwork: This topic includes conversations about social support, friendships, and networks, whether strong or minimal. Example patient statements: 'I have people I can rely on,' 'I don’t have anyone to turn to,' 'My support system is solid.'
SocialEnvironmentalContext.LifeTransitions & Hospitalizations: This topic includes conversations about life transitions (moving, retirement, immigration) and hospitalizations, whether positive, neutral, or difficult. Example patient statements: 'Moving was a great change,' 'Retirement has been hard,' 'I’ve been hospitalized three times.'

CopingGrowth.CopingStrategies & StressManagement: This topic includes conversations about coping and stress management, whether adaptive (exercise, mindfulness) or maladaptive (avoidance, denial). Example patient statements: 'I handle stress by journaling,' 'I avoid problems until they explode,' 'I cope well with challenges.'
CopingGrowth.MindfulnessRelaxation: This topic includes conversations about mindfulness, relaxation, meditation, or other practices, whether practiced regularly or absent. Example patient statements: 'I meditate daily,' 'Relaxation is hard for me,' 'I’ve never tried mindfulness.'
CopingGrowth.MeaningPurpose & HopeForFuture: This topic includes conversations about meaning, life purpose, and hope, whether strong or absent. Example patient statements: 'I feel hopeful about the future,' 'Life feels meaningless,' 'I’ve found purpose in helping others.'
CopingGrowth.SpiritualExistentialConcerns: This topic includes conversations about spiritual beliefs or existential concerns, whether grounding or distressing. Example patient statements: 'Spirituality guides me,' 'I feel disconnected from faith,' 'I question the meaning of life.'
CopingGrowth.CreativityHobbies: This topic includes conversations about creativity, hobbies, and interests, whether fulfilling or lacking. Example patient statements: 'I love painting,' 'I don’t have hobbies,' 'Music brings me joy.'
CopingGrowth.ResiliencePostTraumaticGrowth: This topic includes conversations about resilience and growth after adversity, whether present or lacking. Example patient statements: 'Hard times have made me stronger,' 'I’m resilient in the face of challenges,' 'I don’t feel like I recover from setbacks.'

TherapyProcess.TherapeuticGoals: This topic includes conversations about therapy goals and expectations, whether clear or undefined. Example patient statements: 'I want to feel more stable,' 'I don’t know what I want from therapy.'
TherapyProcess.TherapeuticAlliance & ProgressResistance: This topic includes conversations about the therapeutic relationship, trust, collaboration, or resistance. Example patient statements: 'I trust my therapist,' 'I resist opening up,' 'The alliance feels strong.'
TherapyProcess.ProgressSetbacks: This topic includes conversations about progress in therapy, improvements, or setbacks. Example patient statements: 'I’ve been making progress,' 'Sometimes I regress,' 'Therapy feels like a rollercoaster.'
TherapyProcess.SessionInsights: This topic includes conversations about insights and realizations gained in therapy, whether positive or confusing. Example patient statements: 'I realized something important today,' 'I didn’t understand the exercise,' 'This session helped me see a pattern.'
TherapyProcess.HomeworkPractice: This topic includes conversations about therapy homework, exercises, or practices outside sessions, whether completed or avoided. Example patient statements: 'I did my homework,' 'I skipped the exercise,' 'The practice helped me.'
